body.statement: Can \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{sat}}\) be completed for every finite \((G,\mathcal C,\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\) so that exhaustive sound context-factor recovery either assembles a total \(E\in\mathscr E(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), or produces retained partial-trace rooted C-forests whose jointly quotient-supported multi-block contraction has a kernel direction with zero full observed increment and nonzero query increment, with the binary-sink construction as its exact one-block base case? The resulting procedure must be sound and complete, and on the maximal-regular observed-root subclass it must reduce to the Mokhtarian--Jamshidi--Etesami--Kiyavash criterion while strictly covering inputs with observed endogenous activation.
body.justification: This is the unresolved completeness kernel: multi-district local failures must glue through shared rows into a genuine global query-changing direction or force total arithmetic recovery.
body.gap: Tikka et al. leave general CSI completeness unresolved; Mokhtarian et al. require observed root controls; Chen and Darwiche provide no complete state-specific obstruction theorem.
body.consumer: A positive answer is the missing mathematical basis for a total explanatory CSI-identification backend in \(Y_0\).

obligation.what_is_open: A finite global theorem connecting exhaustive context-compatible factor failure to jointly quotient-supported, multi-block rooted-forest perturbations with zero full observed increment and nonzero full-query increment, together with total arithmetic recovery in every remaining case.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen primitives provide neither a complete normal form for cross-context recovery nor a gluing theorem. A local C-forest does not imply a global direction after quotient row sharing, as the reference-context bow proves; conversely, exhausting an active deletion can erase the only usable forest, as the five-node example proves. Generic real-algebraic feasibility would decide semantic fibers but would not establish the required forest-linked dichotomy or descent to the permitted arithmetic-expression class.
obligation.attempted: The proof was reduced first to retained partial traces and then to row-space tests on residual forest-supported blocks. The one-block fixed-nuisance sink case closes exactly. Extending it by blockwise nullspace intersection fails without controlling changes in nuisance tables and cross-district cancellation; local separating directions can be killed by shared rows, and separate surviving directions need not combine to change the full query.
obligation.partial_result: The exact row quotient, sound SUCCESS assembly, the fixed-nuisance binary-sink affine reduction, its corrected row-space/nullspace alternative, and the positive two-model certificate are proved in this solve. The five-node example proves that maximal active deletion is incomplete, while the bow example proves that a local forest can be annihilated by a shared observed reference context. Thus any future global proof must retain partial traces and solve a jointly shared-row contraction problem whose separating direction changes the full query.
